caveats: **`executeRoles` in the YAML is advisory, not enforced.** Since #1398, raw dispatch authorizes on the compiled `(plugin,action)` pair's securable/operation plus its `ExecuteGate` — `permissions.executeRoles` in `InstructionDefinition` YAML is retired to documentation only (`changelog.d/1398-dispatch-approval-gate.security.md`). Do not treat the Roles row above as an access-control guarantee; the real gate is the Security row.

**`delete_lines`'s output field names don't match its own YAML.** The plugin emits `lines_deleted|total_lines_before|total_lines_after` (`filesystem_plugin.cpp:1997-1999`), but `content/definitions/t2_capabilities.yaml:571-576` declares `lines_deleted`/`lines_before`/`lines_after` — a genuine drift between the shipped result and its own schema. This README's Outputs table uses the runtime field names; `t2_capabilities.yaml` is out of this PR's ownership scope, so the mismatch is flagged here rather than silently "corrected" in either direction.

**`filesystem` and `filesystem_posture` are two different plugins with confusingly similar names.** `filesystem_posture` (`changelog.d/wave6-pr61b-filesystem-posture.added.md`) is a separate, read-only plugin for `mounts`/`quotas`/`snapshots`; two of its test files (`test_filesystem_posture_local_dispatcher.cpp`, `test_filesystem_posture_parsers.cpp`) sit alongside this plugin's own tests in `tests/unit/` and are easy to mistake for filesystem's own coverage. They are not — see *Source and tests*.

**No test loads the real built plugin through `LocalDispatcher`.** Unlike `filesystem_posture`'s dispatcher test, `test_filesystem_actions.cpp` and `test_filesystem_read.cpp` both replicate the plugin's helper logic (`validate_path`, `glob_match`, `atomic_write_file`, etc.) in the test TU's own anonymous namespace rather than linking or loading `filesystem.dylib`/`.so`/`.dll` (`tests/unit/test_filesystem_actions.cpp:12-13`, `tests/unit/test_filesystem_read.cpp:5-6`) — a regression in the real `.cpp` that the replica doesn't share would not be caught by these suites.

**macOS/Linux `get_signature`/`get_version_info`'s TOCTOU re-check is a narrowing, not a fix.** The BR-006 comments in the code say so explicitly: an unprivileged writer inside `base_dir` can still win a race between the re-validate call and codesign's/plutil's own `open()`, because both are path-based external tools (`filesystem_plugin.cpp:1206-1223`, `:1469-1483`). `base_dir` must not be writable by lower-privileged principals.

definitions.description: Append text content to the end of an existing file. Optionally adds a newline separator if the file does not end with one. The file must already exist and be a regular file. Paths are canonicalized; optional base_dir restricts access.

Create a secure temporary file on the endpoint with restrictive permissions (mode 0600 on POSIX, owner-only DACL on Windows). Uses mkstemps/CreateFile+CREATE_NEW to prevent TOCTOU races. Optionally deletes the file immediately (persist=false) for use as a unique path generator.

Create a secure temporary directory on the endpoint with restrictive permissions (mode 0700 on POSIX, owner-only DACL on Windows). Optionally deletes the directory immediately (persist=false) for use as a unique path generator.

Delete a range of lines (1-based, inclusive) from a text file. Reads the entire file, removes the specified lines, and writes it back atomically. Files larger than 100 MB are rejected. The start_line must not exceed the total number of lines; end_line is clamped if it goes past the end.

Check whether a filesystem path exists on the endpoint. Reports the existence, type (file, directory, other), and size. Paths are canonicalized via std::filesystem::canonical() to resolve symlinks. An optional base_dir parameter restricts access to a subtree.

Compute the SHA-256 (default) or SHA-1 hash of a file on the endpoint. Uses BCrypt on Windows and sha256sum/shasum on POSIX. Files larger than 10 GB are rejected. Returns the hex digest, algorithm used, and file size in bytes.

Search a directory tree for files matching a specific SHA256 hash. Useful for IOC hunting, malware detection, and file integrity verification. Walks the directory recursively up to the specified depth limit. Returns matching file paths and sizes.

Retrieve access control list (ACL) or permissions for a file or directory. On Windows, returns the SDDL representation and individual ACE entries (allow/deny, account, access mask). On Linux/macOS, returns POSIX owner, group, and permission mode (rwxrwxrwx).

Verify the code signature of an executable, DLL, or app bundle. On Windows, uses WinVerifyTrust to check the Authenticode signature chain (valid, unsigned, distrusted, untrusted). On macOS, runs `codesign --verify --deep --strict` and reports an honest macOS signature status (valid, unsigned, invalid, unknown) — a different vocabulary from Authenticode, since codesign/Gatekeeper model trust differently than WinVerifyTrust. On macOS, `valid` means the code signature's seal is INTACT (integrity: the binary/bundle is unmodified since signing) — it does NOT mean the signer is trusted, notarized, or accepted by Gatekeeper; an ad-hoc or self-signed binary reports `valid`. This is a weaker assurance than the Windows `valid`, which also validates the certificate chain to a trusted root. Returns error on Linux.

Extract version information from an executable or app bundle. On Windows, reads the PE version resource (FileVersion, ProductVersion, and descriptive fields such as CompanyName/FileDescription/ProductName) and returns an error if the file carries no version resource. On macOS, reads CFBundleVersion and CFBundleShortVersionString from the bundle's Info.plist via `plutil -extract ... raw` — plutil handles both binary and XML plists, so this works on any .app regardless of how its Info.plist is encoded — and reports an honest version_status|not_available when the target has no Info.plist or no version keys within it, rather than failing. Returns error on Linux.

List the contents of a directory on the endpoint, up to 1000 entries. Reports each entry's filename, type (file, directory, symlink, other), and size. Paths are canonicalized; optional base_dir restricts access.

Read lines from a text file on the endpoint with pagination support. Returns lines with 1-based line numbers, total line count, and file size. Binary files are detected and rejected. Maximum file size is 100 MB, maximum lines per request is 10000. Paths are canonicalized; optional base_dir restricts access.

Find and replace text in a file using literal string matching or regex. Supports case-insensitive mode, dry-run (preview without writing), and a maximum replacement count. The write is atomic (temp file + rename) to prevent corruption. Files larger than 100 MB are rejected. Regex patterns with nested quantifiers are rejected for safety.

Search a text file's contents for lines matching a literal string or regex pattern. Returns matching line numbers and content. Supports case-insensitive search, regex mode with backtracking protection, and configurable maximum match count. Files larger than 100 MB are rejected.

Search a directory tree for files or directories matching a name pattern. Supports both glob matching (default) and regex. Walks the tree recursively up to max_depth with configurable result limits. Paths are canonicalized; optional base_dir restricts the search scope.

Write or create a file with the specified content. If the file exists, overwrite must be true. If the file does not exist, create must be true. Content is written atomically for existing files (temp + rename) to prevent corruption. Maximum content size is 100 MB. Paths are canonicalized; optional base_dir restricts access.

Two-step workflow that first searches for lines matching a pattern in a configuration file to confirm the current value, then performs a find/replace operation to update it. The search step uses dry-run semantics (no changes), and the replace step performs the actual modification with an atomic write. Designed for configuration drift remediation.
definitions.display_name: Workflow: Search Config and Replace Value

definitions.description: Compliance workflow that retrieves the PE version information of a Windows executable and evaluates it against a minimum required version. Designed to be chained with inventory evaluation: the get_version_info result populates inventory data, then a PolicyFragment with a version_gte condition triggers remediation if the version is below the threshold. On non-Windows platforms, uses the filesystem.exists action as a fallback check.

description: Filesystem operations — exists, list_dir, file_hash, search_dir, text ops (admin-only)
how_it_works:
Every action funnels its `path`/`root`/`directory` parameter through `validate_path` or `validate_path_or_parent`, which resolve symlinks via `fs::canonical` and, when `base_dir` is set, refuse anything that resolves outside it (`filesystem_plugin.cpp:101-184`). Reads never touch the target; the four write actions (`replace`, `write_content` on an existing file, `delete_lines`) go through `atomic_write_file` — write to a same-directory temp file, then rename (`filesystem_plugin.cpp:391-415`) — while `append`, `create_temp`, `create_temp_dir`, and a fresh `write_content` open the target directly. `file_hash`/`find_by_hash` hash in-process via BCrypt on Windows (`compute_hash_win`, `filesystem_plugin.cpp:188-245`) and by exec'ing an absolute-path `sha256sum`/`sha1sum`/`shasum` through the bounded subprocess runner on POSIX, never a shell (`compute_hash_unix`, `filesystem_plugin.cpp:249-316`). `get_signature`/`get_version_info` are Windows/macOS-only: native `WinVerifyTrust`/`GetFileVersionInfoW` calls on Windows (`filesystem_plugin.cpp:1154-1206`, `:1389-1453`), `/usr/bin/codesign`/`/usr/bin/plutil` exec'd through the same runner on macOS, each preceded by a BR-006 immediate re-validate-before-exec check that narrows (but does not eliminate) a TOCTOU window (`filesystem_plugin.cpp:1206-1223`, `:1463-1483`); both report an honest unsupported/`not_available` result on Linux (`filesystem_plugin.cpp:1262-1265`, `:1550-1553`). `search_dir`/`search`/`replace` share a ReDoS guard that rejects nested-quantifier regexes (`has_nested_quantifiers`, `filesystem_plugin.cpp:322-345`); `search_dir`'s glob mode uses a hand-rolled matcher (`glob_match`, `filesystem_plugin.cpp:349-387`).

The plugin deliberately never calls a typed result-status setter — no `set_result_status`/`yuzu_ctx_set_result_status` call exists anywhere in `filesystem_plugin.cpp` — so every action's outcome is carried entirely in its pipe-delimited rows and return code; see *Result status* below. It also deliberately stops at line-range deletion and ACL *reads*: there is no whole-file delete, no rename, and no ACL/DACL *write* action anywhere in the action list.

outputs_note: Every action writes pipe-delimited `key|value` lines via `ctx.write_output()`. A *repeating* row (`list_dir`'s entries, Windows `get_acl`'s ACEs, `search`/`search_dir`/`find_by_hash`'s matches, `read`'s lines) is prefixed with a literal discriminator word naming the row's kind, then its fields; a single-value field is its own `key|value` line with no discriminator. There is no shared placeholder row for "found nothing" — a zero-hit action reports only its trailing count (`total_matches|0`, `matches_found|0`) with no rows above it. Failure is always a single `error|<message>` line plus a non-zero return code, never a placeholder success row (see *Result status*).

privileges.grant: None for any read action. `write_content`/`replace`/`append`/`delete_lines` against a path the running account cannot already write need that account to be an `Administrators` member; default install grants nothing (`docs/agent-privilege-model.md:118`)
privileges.if_refused: a single `error|<message>` line + return code 1 (e.g. `error|GetNamedSecurityInfo failed (error N)`) — no typed status is set
privileges.runs_as: **LocalSystem today** (`docs/agent-privilege-model.md:70`, tracked #1442; target is the virtual service account `NT SERVICE\YuzuAgent`)

privileges.grant: None for any read action. Write actions against a path with no operator-authored per-path sudo entry are refused by the OS itself at `open()`/`rename()`; default install grants nothing (`docs/agent-privilege-model.md:118`)

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result only.** Rows travel over the agent's mTLS gRPC channel as the command response and land in the ResponseStore (90-day default retention, `server/core/src/response_store.hpp:8,152`), queryable at `/api/responses/{id}`.

**Not consumed by** daily-sync inventory, the TAR warehouse, DEX, or metrics — grepping the server tree for `device.filesystem.` and for the plugin name outside the capability catalogue and generic result-parsing table (`server/core/src/result_parsing.hpp:66`) finds no sync-source, TAR, or DEX consumer. Nothing runs on a schedule; the plugin executes only when an operator or workflow dispatches one of its 16 definitions.

**Sensitivity.** `get_acl` rows carry local account names (POSIX `owner`/`group`, Windows ACE `account` — potentially real usernames, not just built-in principals) and `get_version_info`/`get_signature` rows name specific installed software (`company_name`, `product_name`, `file_description`) — an installed-software inventory by another route; every action's `path`/`content` fields carry whatever the operator pointed at, which can include usernames embedded in home-directory paths or arbitrary personal data in file contents.

**Siblings:** `filesystem_posture.mounts`/`.quotas`/`.snapshots` — a separate, similarly-named, read-only plugin (mount/quota/snapshot inventory only; no read-file, hash, or write actions) — do not confuse the two (see Caveats). Two shipped workflow definitions chain this plugin's actions: `workflow.config_search_and_replace` (`content/definitions/t2_chaining_examples.yaml:15`) searches a config file then dispatches `filesystem.replace`, and `workflow.version_compliance_check` (`content/definitions/t2_chaining_examples.yaml:206`) dispatches `filesystem.get_version_info` and compares the result against a minimum version.

**MCP / REST.** Discover: `discover_plugins` (summary) → `yuzu://plugin-docs` (this page as data) → `discover_instructions` / `get_definition("device.filesystem.file_hash")`. Run: `execute_instruction {definition_id, parameters}`. Read: `/api/responses/{id}`.
